products.name: Real-Time CDP Collaboration
products.what: With Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration, you can discover, activate, and measure high-value audiences without relying on third-party cookies.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration overview

lines.name: Collaboration access and roles setup
lines.scope: Grant administrator access, create Permissions roles that include the View Profiles and View Segments permissions audience sourcing needs, add sandboxes, assign users and confirm each one can open Collaboration.
lines.evidence: Your organization's access roles determine what users can see and do in Collaboration.

source.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide

lines.name: Account, branding and match key setup
lines.scope: Agree the match key strategy with your client, create the advertiser or publisher account, add the name, description, logo and contact email, and configure the match keys used to align audiences.
lines.evidence: Define your account's role in Collaboration, provide branding assets, and configure match keys to align audiences across connections.

source.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide

lines.name: Audience sourcing from cloud data sources
lines.scope: For audiences kept outside Experience Platform, prepare files to Adobe's audience specification with SHA256-hashed identifiers and the required metadata, then set up the Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage or Snowflake data connection.
lines.evidence: Cloud-based audience files must follow the required schema outlined in the Audience Specification PDF.

source.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide

lines.name: Collaborator connections and first projects
lines.scope: Find publishers in the Connect workspace or send private invitations, agree connection settings such as use cases and credit consumption, confirm the connection and set up the first project with Discover, Activate and Measure.
lines.evidence: involves sending or receiving invitations, reviewing and submitting connection settings (such as use cases and credit consumption)

source.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide

lines.name: Overlap and measurement reporting enablement
lines.scope: Train your client's team to read audience overlap insights, pick audiences to activate, add campaign IDs and create campaign summary and attribution reports in the Measure workspace.
lines.evidence: Get insight into overlap percentages and the number of overlapping identities between your audiences and those of your collaborators.

source.title: Experience League: Collaboration use cases

lines.name: Monthly collaboration operations
lines.scope: Each month, add or retire audiences, tune refresh schedules to manage credit use, set up projects for new campaigns and run overlap and measurement reports with collaborators.
lines.evidence: You can add or remove audiences and update the refresh schedule directly in Collaboration.

source.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide

products.name: Mix Modeler
products.what: Marketing Campaign Analytics is an Adobe Experience Cloud application that measures campaigns and optimizes planning holistically across all channels: paid, earned, and owned.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics guide (formerly Mix Modeler)

lines.name: Access, roles and sandbox setup
lines.scope: Create the Permissions role with the Marketing Campaign Analytics resource and its harmonized data, model and plan permissions, add the sandboxes and dataset and schema permissions, and assign users.
lines.evidence: For Marketing Campaign Analytics to function properly, you must set the correct permissions.

source.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics administration

lines.name: Marketing data ingestion and schemas
lines.scope: Model schemas on the XDM ExperienceEvent or Summary Metrics classes, then ingest channel spend and effort, conversions and internal and external factors with consistent dates, granularity and channel fields, and validate the loads.
lines.evidence: Date and granularity are mandatory fields in the underlying schema for all aggregate data ingested as datasets

source.title: Experience League: Ingest data overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)

lines.name: Harmonized data, touchpoints and conversions
lines.scope: Define harmonized fields, write dataset rules for each aggregate, event and factor dataset, define marketing touchpoints and conversions, then sync and check the harmonized data.
lines.evidence: Set up dataset rules to map fields from your aggregate (factor or summary) or experience event datasets to harmonized fields.

source.title: Experience League: Harmonize datasets overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)

lines.name: Model build, training and validation
lines.scope: Configure models with the conversion, touchpoints, lookback and training windows, factors and priors, turn on multi-touch attribution or full funnel modeling where agreed, and retrain until the fit suits the business.
lines.evidence: Retraining and rescoring are an iterative process as new findings and information emerge and adjustments are needed

source.title: Experience League: Models overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)

lines.name: Budget plans and team enablement
lines.scope: Build the first budget plans with flight dates and channel constraints, compare scenarios, and train marketing and finance users to read model and plan insights.
lines.evidence: Plans in Marketing Campaign Analytics allow you to allocate budgets by business unit and channel.

source.title: Experience League: Plans overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)

lines.name: Monthly data refresh, rescoring and plans
lines.scope: Each month, load new spend, conversion and factor data, rescore or retrain models, rebuild plans on the rescored models and report ROI and budget shifts to stakeholders.
lines.evidence: data may be added to the model which requires you to rescore the model manually.

source.title: Experience League: Models overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)

notes: Mix Modeler has been renamed Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics. Every Experience League page in its guide (updated Oct 29 2026) says it 'is the evolution and rebranding of Adobe Mix Modeler', and business.adobe.com titles the product 'Marketing Campaign Analytics (formerly Mix Modeler)'. Doc URLs still use /mix-modeler/. The id stays mmm and the name stays Mix Modeler as asked; consider showing 'Marketing Campaign Analytics (formerly Mix Modeler)' on the canvas.

Collaboration availability: every Collaboration page carries a Limited Availability badge and says it 'is currently available in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, with global availability coming soon.' It needs its own Collaboration license; a Starter user can join only when invited by a partner that holds a Real-Time CDP Prime, Ultimate or Collaboration license, in the same region. Activities consume credits.

Collaboration limits from the quick start: advertisers can source up to 25 audiences, publishers up to 250 (each with at least 1,000 IDs). Self-serve destinations are Experience Platform only; cloud destinations are set up by Adobe on request. Full measurement reporting 'may require backend enablement', and measurement data can only come from Experience Platform today.
Collaboration measurement (XD03) is marked optional in Adobe's quick start, so it defaults off, but attribution reports in the Measure workspace cannot run without it.

collab-cja and collab-mmm rest on one bullet on the Collaboration product page: 'Export campaign performance data to measurement partners and tools, including Adobe Customer Journey Analytics and Adobe Mix Modeler for deeper analysis and media planning.' The sentence ends with an asterisk, and the only asterisk footnote on the page reads 'Coming soon'. No Experience League page describes this export. Consider hiding these two lines until Adobe documents the export.

Mix Modeler license terms: the helpx product description (effective Aug 13 2024, still under the Mix Modeler name) says Privacy and Security Shield must be licensed with Mix Modeler, and that the license includes up to 5 sandboxes and 10 active models. Check current terms before quoting.

Mix Modeler full funnel modeling: the Models overview still shows a Limited Testing note, while the Oct 2026 release notes list it as generally available on Oct 29 2026. MM04 treats it as optional. Event-level scores, used in XD07 and XD08, exist only when multi-touch attribution is turned on for the model.

Real-Time CDP lookalikes (XD04): Real-Time CDP Prime includes 5 and Ultimate 20 active look-alike audiences in production sandboxes. The base audience must be created in Experience Platform on the default merge policy, and look-alike features switch off automatically in low-usage environments. Collaboration also has a Beta Expand tab for expansion audiences built from a collaborator's population; it is not used in these lines.

Content Analytics and CJA: Adobe's Content Analytics product page answers 'Is Adobe Customer Journey Analytics required?' with 'No.', yet Experience League runs Content Analytics configuration and reporting inside CJA (connection, data view, Workspace template). The cja-ca lines assume the client also licenses CJA with its own journey data. Confirm what a Content Analytics-only license includes, including audience publishing for XD06 (which therefore needs cja).

Content Analytics limits from Experience League: featurization is English only, it is not a HIPAA-ready service, Privacy and Security Shield labeling does not cover its experiences and assets, and the paid media channel is not available for CJA and Experience Platform deployments on AWS. Paid media supports Meta and Google, with Pinterest, Snapchat and TikTok in Limited Testing.

The Google Ads (V2) source page says 'The Google Ads source is available as part of the Customer Journey Analytics SKU.' The Meta Ads source page was listed as Beta in search results. Its use-case table says it feeds ad datasets 'to Adobe Mix Modeler via Snowflake', which is unclear, so XD10 rests on the Marketing Campaign Analytics product pages instead.

ca-gspm channel overlap: GenStudio activates to Meta, LinkedIn, Campaign Manager 360 and other channels, and its own Insights covers Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, DV360 and Innovid. Content Analytics paid media covers Meta and Google. Today the measurable overlap is mainly Meta; LinkedIn ads made in GenStudio do not reach Content Analytics.

GenStudio's own Insights also analyzes paid media attributes. Adobe's Content Analytics FAQ draws the line: GenStudio for Performance Marketing 'is for creating, activating, and optimizing paid media content at scale', and Content Analytics 'is for measuring how that content performs and tying it to business outcomes'.

GenStudio availability: generation supports 12 GA languages plus 5 in Beta, translation covers 40+ languages, and text features are English only (release notes). AEM Assets is the default DAM and Workfront Proof integration exists, but neither is on this canvas, so GS03 assumes assets are loaded into Content. The helpx GenStudio product description could not be read (the fetch permission timed out), so license limits are unverified.

Overlaps checked against the other helper's Content Analytics lines (portal_omnichannel_b2b.json): tracking-key mapping for paid media is left to CA04 (no cja-ca line repeats it), XD12 covers only the review of existing data views that CA02's guided configuration does not, and XD13 extends the template CA05 sets up. Elsewhere, XD06 (content audiences) is a content-specific case of RC03 (journey audiences from CJA), and XD05 and XD09 both reuse Experience Platform event data in Mix Modeler, from different apps.
Connections with one flow (rtcdp-ca, collab-mmm, collab-cja) list only the direction Adobe documents.

business.adobe.com pages refuse script downloads here, so their quotes (Collaboration, Marketing Campaign Analytics, paid media analysis, Content Analytics and GenStudio product pages) were read and rechecked through WebFetch, not by script. Every Experience League quote was script-checked against the downloaded page.
Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
